## Project Overview

**Project:** `travel-assist`
**Language:** Kotlin (primary)
**Framework:** Spring Boot 4.0.4 with Spring Data JPA, Spring Modulith, Spring Web, Netflix DGS Codegen, Jackson Kotlin Module, and GraalVM Native Image support
**Build System:** Gradle (Kotlin DSL — `build.gradle.kts`)
**Entry Point:** `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/TravelAssistApplication.kt`

This is a Spring Boot REST API for managing travel trips. It exposes CRUD operations for `Trip` resources under `/api/trips`, persists data to an H2 in-memory database via Spring Data JPA, and is structured using Spring Modulith for modular boundaries. It is an early-stage project — GraphQL client generation via Netflix DGS Codegen is configured but schemas may not yet be present. Docker Compose integration is scaffolded via `compose.yaml`.

## Safe Operations

These are operations an agent is explicitly permitted to perform. When in doubt, stop and ask rather than proceed.

- **Add new REST endpoints** to `TripController` (`src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/controller/TripController.kt`) following the existing `@GetMapping` / `@PostMapping` / `@PutMapping` / `@DeleteMapping` patterns already present in that class.
- **Add new fields** to the `Trip` entity (`src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/model/Trip.kt`) and its corresponding `TripDto` (`src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/dto/TripDto.kt`), with matching updates propagated through `TripService` and `TripController`.
- **Add new service classes** in `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/service/` annotated with `@Service`, following the pattern of `TripService`.
- **Add new repository interfaces** in `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/repository/` extending `JpaRepository`, following the pattern of `TripRepository`.
- **Add new DTO classes** in `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/dto/` using Kotlin data classes with Jakarta validation annotations as needed.
- **Add new model/entity classes** in `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/model/` as JPA entities using `@Entity` and `@Table`.
- **Add new test classes** in `src/test/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/` using JUnit 5. Match the package structure of the class under test.
- **Modify `application.properties` or `application.yml`** for configuration changes. Be aware both files exist — see the pitfall about conflicting keys before editing.

## Domain Glossary

These are the core business and technical concepts in this codebase. Understand these before reading or writing any domain logic.

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Trip** | The central domain entity. Represents a single travel trip planned by a user. Stored in the `trips` database table. Fields include `title`, `description`, `destination`, and a date range (start/end dates). Persisted via JPA. |
| **TripDto** | A Data Transfer Object used as the request body when creating or updating a `Trip`. It is a Kotlin data class carrying the same logical fields as `Trip` but decorated with Jakarta validation annotations (e.g., `title` must not be blank). It is not persisted directly — the service maps it to a `Trip` entity. |
| **TripRepository** | A Spring Data JPA interface extending `JpaRepository<Trip, Long>` (or equivalent). It provides all standard database operations — `save`, `findById`, `findAll`, `deleteById` — without requiring any implementation code. This is the only point of direct database interaction. |
| **TripService** | The service layer class annotated with `@Service`. It contains all business logic for trip operations and is the only place where `TripRepository` should be called. Methods are `@Transactional` where mutations occur. Controllers must go through this class — never call the repository directly from a controller. |
| **TripController** | The REST controller annotated with `@RestController` and mapped to `/api/trips`. It receives HTTP requests, delegates to `TripService`, and returns HTTP responses. It owns request/response mapping but no business logic. It uses `TripDto` as input and returns either `Trip` entities or response wrappers. |

## Potential Pitfalls

These are known risks and sharp edges in this specific codebase. Read each one before making changes in the relevant area.

> **⚠ Spring Boot 4.0.4 is cutting-edge.**
> This project targets Spring Boot 4.0.4, which is a very recent version. Third-party plugins and libraries may not yet have compatible releases. Before adding any new dependency or plugin, verify it explicitly supports Spring Boot 4.x. Do not upgrade or downgrade the Spring Boot version without explicit human instruction.

> **⚠ Kotlin data classes as JPA entities are fragile.**
> The `Trip` entity in `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/model/Trip.kt` is a Kotlin data class used as a JPA entity. The `id` field is `val` (immutable, correct) and other fields are `var` (mutable, required by JPA). Do not change `var` fields to `val`, do not add a no-arg constructor manually, and do not make the class `final` or sealed. JPA requires mutable state and proxying ability. The `kotlin-allopen` and `kotlin-noarg` plugins handle this — do not remove them from `build.gradle.kts`.

> **⚠ The DGS Codegen `generateJava` task may fail.**
> The Netflix DGS Codegen plugin is configured and expects GraphQL schema files in `src/main/resources/graphql-client/`. This directory may not yet exist. If `./gradlew build` fails on the `generateJava` task, it is because the schema directory or `.graphql` files are missing — not a code bug. Do not remove the plugin to fix this; create the directory or add a stub schema instead.

> **⚠ H2 is the only database — there is no production configuration.**
> The only database dependency is H2 at runtime scope. There is no `application-prod.yml`, no Flyway or Liquibase migration setup, and no external database driver. Do not assume a production database exists. Do not switch from H2 to PostgreSQL, MySQL, or any other database unless explicitly instructed, and only do so with a complete configuration change including connection properties and a new driver dependency.

> **⚠ `compose.yaml` exists but its contents are unknown.**
> A `compose.yaml` file is present, suggesting Spring Boot Docker Compose
